approachQuestion.prompt:
Storage Check
Return true exactly when array A represents a binary min-heap: every parent value is at most each existing child. Children of i have indices 2i+1 and 2i+2. Duplicates are allowed. Example: [1,4,2,7,5] → true; [1,4,2,3] → false; [] → true.

0 ≤ n=len(A) ≤ 200000; signed 32-bit values. Input is read-only; return one boolean. No heap validity promise is given. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 0 ≤ n=len(A) ≤ 200000; signed 32-bit values. Input is read-only; return one boolean. No heap validity promise is given.

options.text: For every nonroot index j, compare A[j] with A[(j−1)//2]. Return false on the first smaller child; otherwise return true.
options.feedback: Every required parent-child inequality is checked exactly once. Those local inequalities are the definition of a heap; sibling order is irrelevant.

options.text: For every parent index, compare it with each child whose index is in bounds; return false for a smaller child and true if none exists.
options.feedback: This checks precisely the same set of inequalities with constant working state.

options.text: Return true only if the full array is nondecreasing from left to right.
options.feedback: The valid example [1,4,2,7,5] is not globally sorted; siblings need not be ordered.

options.text: Recursively verify the left and right subtrees and their links to each parent, keeping one call frame per depth.
options.feedback: The checks are correct, but recursion retains a call stack that an index scan avoids.

feedback.reason: Every required parent-child inequality is checked exactly once. Those local inequalities are the definition of a heap; sibling order is irrelevant.
details: For every nonroot index j, compare A[j] with A[(j−1)//2]. Return false on the first smaller child; otherwise return true.

Heap order is a local parent-child property that must hold for every nonroot index. Sortedness is stronger and unnecessary. Even a valid heap requires inspecting every link to rule out a late violation.

“For every nonroot index j, compare A[j] with A[(j−1)//2]. Return false on the first smaller child; otherwise return true.”: Every required parent-child inequality is checked exactly once. Those local inequalities are the definition of a heap; sibling order is irrelevant.

“For every parent index, compare it with each child whose index is in bounds; return false for a smaller child and true if none exists.”: This checks precisely the same set of inequalities with constant working state.
“Return true only if the full array is nondecreasing from left to right.”: The valid example [1,4,2,7,5] is not globally sorted; siblings need not be ordered.

“Recursively verify the left and right subtrees and their links to each parent, keeping one call frame per depth.”: The checks are correct, but recursion retains a call stack that an index scan avoids.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A specifically, an iterative loop over j=1 through n−1 with early exit on a violation. Let n be array length. Do not copy the input; count worst-case inputs including valid heaps. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: A valid array forces n-1 comparisons with only scalar index state.
details: A valid heap requires checking all n−1 links, yielding O(n) worst-case time and only an index and a few values as state. Empty and singleton arrays are accepted without a comparison. Tree height does not reduce the number of links that must be inspected.
“O(log(n+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Height bounds one repair path, while this verification checks every link.
“O(n) time, O(log(n+1)) auxiliary space”: This is recursive traversal storage; A is iterative.
“O(n log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: No sorting, rebuilding, or copied heap is used.
